note: Outside forecasts of when AGI arrives, plotted against our AGI-anywhere curve (definitions v2.0). None uses our exact definition. Each entry's bar says how it compares with definitions v2.0: announcement (measures an announcement, not whether a system exists), narrower (an easier milestone, so an early bound), stricter (a harder milestone, so a late bound), different (a different test) or own-definition (the forecaster's own, unstated bar); gap says how in one line. barV1 and gapV1 keep the comparison with the v1.0 strict bar. A median is plotted as a 50% point at that date. Market prices come from the market's public API, dated in Pacific time.

forecasts.what: Automated coder, median (no later than May 2027, his superhuman-AI-researcher median)
forecasts.definition: Automated coder (AC): an AI that can fully automate coding in an AGI project; narrower than our bar (coding only), so an early bound. The AI Futures Project's Q3.5 Timelines Update (Nov 10, 2026) gives no new AC median for him; it puts his median for a superhuman AI researcher (SAR) at May 2027, and a SAR 'must also qualify as an Automated Coder', so his AC median can be no later than May 2027. We plot it at 50% at that bound, which if anything understates his chance of AC by then (our inference). In August his all-things-considered AC median was Nov 2027 in two of the Q2.5 update's charts and Dec 2027 in a third; in the Q3.5 post he recalls it as December 2027. The authors judge it 'unlikely but not totally implausible' that AC has already been reached. The forecast assumes no more deliberate slowing than in the recent past.
forecasts.gap: Coding only, so it should arrive before a system meets our definition.
forecasts.rating: expert opinion (AI Futures Project, Q3.5 Timelines Update, Nov 10, 2026; the AC bound from his SAR median is our inference)
forecasts.gapV1: Coding only, so it should arrive before our bar.

forecasts.what: First weakly general AI system, community median
forecasts.definition: Metaculus weakly-general-AI question (Q3479): one unified, publicly announced system that reliably passes a Loebner-Silver-Prize-type Turing test, scores 90% or more on Winogrande or a comparable set, reaches the 75th percentile on a circa-2015-2020 SAT math section from page images, and learns Montezuma's Revenge well enough to explore all 24 rooms within the equivalent of 100 hours of play.
forecasts.gap: Four fixed tests that a typical college-educated person finds easy, with no professional-work, multi-week or reliability test, so an early bound. It needs a public announcement, so it can never count a hidden system.
forecasts.rating: forecast aggregate (Metaculus community prediction, read on the question page at 13:23 PT Nov 13, 2026; about 1.8k forecasters; middle half 24 Sep 2026 to 16 Sep 2029, from the page's Community row)

forecasts.definition: Top-expert-dominating AI: AIs better than top human experts at virtually all tasks, which the AI Futures Project's Q3.5 Timelines Update (Nov 10, 2026) also describes as AIs that can automate all white-collar work. In that update his TED-AI median moves to Sep 2027 from Nov 2028 in August, and he puts 65% on TED-AI before 2028. The authors say the single biggest source of evidence was METR's recent assessment of AI R&D acceleration at Anthropic, which they read as a 1.7x AI-attributable speed-up in the pace of progress; METR says Anthropic redacted a majority of the evidence it found most informative (METR, via AI Futures). The forecast assumes no more deliberate slowing ('pacing the frontier') than in the recent past. Stricter than our bar, so a late bound; the month is plotted at mid-month.
forecasts.gap: Top-expert level on virtually all cognitive tasks, so it should arrive after a system meets our definition.
forecasts.rating: expert opinion (AI Futures Project, Q3.5 Timelines Update, Nov 10, 2026, its forecast table and appendix; METR's words via AI Futures)
forecasts.gapV1: Top-expert level on virtually all cognitive tasks, so it should arrive after our bar.

forecasts.what: Full recursive self-improvement (automated AI R&D) possible, now more likely in 2027 than 2028
forecasts.definition: In Import AI 455 (May 4, 2026) he put a "likely chance (60%+)" on no-human-involved AI R&D, an AI system that could plausibly build its own successor autonomously, by the end of 2028, and 30% on it for 2027. In Import AI 476 (Oct 12, 2026) he wrote that he now thinks it "more likely we'll see full RSI become possible in 2027", where before he thought 2028 more likely. He gave no new probability, and the text of his Oct 17 IMF lecture (Import AI 477) gives none either. We plot it at 50% at the end of 2027 as an approximation, as for Hassabis.
forecasts.gap: AI research only, and "possible" rather than done or deployed, so it should come before a system meets our definition; it is closer to our hypothesis B (hidden self-improvement) than to AGI and says nothing about whether it would be hidden.
forecasts.rating: expert opinion (Anthropic co-founder; his own newsletter, Import AI 476, Oct 12, 2026, and Import AI 455, May 4, 2026)

forecasts.what: Artificial superintelligence absent a strong governance intervention, forecasters' median
forecasts.definition: Sentinel's Global Risks Weekly Roundup #45/2026 (Nov 9, 2026) asks: "Absent a strong governance intervention, when will artificial superintelligence (ASI) be developed?" Its forecasters' 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles are 2027.2, 2028.2 and 2047.5, with ranges of 2026 to 2027.5, 2027.5 to 2029 and 2032 to 2085 in brackets, which we read as the spread of individual forecasts (our inference). Strong interventions could include a months-long pause voluntarily agreed by the frontier companies, but not liability or killswitch requirements. The post does not define ASI or say how many forecasters answered or how their figures were combined. Its forecasters call METR's report on Anthropic a big update, tempered because the acceleration is on "well-specified tasks". Their earlier medians were 2040 (Jul 2025) and 2031 (Apr 2026), via the AI Futures Project's Q3.5 update, not checked in Sentinel's archive. We plot 2028.2 as Mar 14, 2028 (our inference).
forecasts.gap: Superintelligence, which the post leaves undefined but which goes beyond top-human level, so it should come after a system meets our definition; it assumes no strong governance intervention.
forecasts.rating: forecast aggregate (Sentinel's forecasting team, Global Risks Weekly Roundup #45/2026, Nov 9, 2026; a small team whose size and aggregation method the post does not state for this question)

forecasts.what: Automated AI researcher by March 2028, stated goal

A goal, not a probability; plotted at 50% as an approximation, as for Hassabis.
forecasts.gap: AI research only, and under human supervision, so it should come before a system meets our definition; it is closer to our hypothesis B (hidden self-improvement) than to AGI. A stated goal, not a probability.
forecasts.rating: expert opinion (lab's own stated goal, from OpenAI's Sept 6, 2026 post; the intern milestone is OpenAI's own measurement)

forecasts.definition: On LinkedIn on Dec 11, 2025, the day his interview with Hannah Fry aired on Google DeepMind: The Podcast, he put a 50% chance on AGI by 2028, a prediction he says he has held for well over a decade. In the interview he calls this level minimal AGI, an artificial agent that can handle the cognitive tasks most people typically do, with full AGI (the entire range of human cognition) three to six years later (via The Decoder). The year is plotted at mid-year.
forecasts.gap: The cognitive tasks a typical person does, an easier bar than our definition's full scope at a skilled professional's level, so an early bound. His full AGI, three to six years later, is closer to ours.
forecasts.rating: expert opinion (lab leader; 50% by 2028 from his own LinkedIn post; the minimal-AGI definition via The Decoder, not checked against the audio)
forecasts.gapV1: Typical-human level across all cognitive tasks, against our skilled-professional level on 80% of remote work; neither is clearly easier.

forecasts.what: AGI within two to three years (reported Oct 2026)
forecasts.definition: His own definition, which The Decoder gives as a system matching the full cognitive range of the human brain. WSJ. Magazine's profile by Ben Cohen (Oct 21, 2026), which names Hassabis its technology innovator this year, reports that he now expects AGI within two to three years, as relayed by The Decoder, TechTimes and t2ONLINE; they give the figure without quotation marks, and we could not read the paywalled WSJ text. In May 2026 he had predicted AGI by 2029 or 2030 (via Sherwood News, relaying Axios). He gives no probability; we plot it at 50% at the window's midpoint (Apr 2029) as an approximation.
forecasts.gap: His own definition, close in scope to ours as The Decoder describes it, with no stated test or probability; the two-to-three-year window reaches us secondhand, not in his quoted words.
forecasts.rating: expert opinion (lab leader; via The Decoder, Oct 21, 2026, relaying WSJ. Magazine (Ben Cohen); the WSJ text was paywalled and the relaying outlets give the two-to-three-year figure without quotation marks, so his exact words are unchecked)
forecasts.gapV1: His own definition and a two-year point estimate, not a probability.

forecasts.what: Powerful AI widely available within a few years, company belief
forecasts.definition: In its S-1 registration statement, filed with the SEC on Oct 26, 2026, Anthropic writes: "We believe that Powerful AI, a highly capable and impactful form of frontier AI characterized by the following key attributes, will become widely available within a few years". The attributes are cognitive capabilities "matching or exceeding those of top human experts across most professional and scientific disciplines"; navigating every interface available to a human working virtually; reasoning through complex tasks autonomously "over extended periods—lasting hours, days, or weeks"; coordinating across instances and with humans and other AI systems; and controlling lab equipment, robots and other machines through digital connections. Its first amendment (S-1/A, accepted on EDGAR at 06:24 PT Nov 2, 2026) repeats the same sentence; its second (S-1/A, accepted at 03:29 PT Nov 10, 2026) keeps "will become widely available within a few years" and the same attributes, but calls Powerful AI "a highly capable and impactful form of frontier intelligence" instead of "frontier AI", and speaks of collaborating with "other systems" instead of "other AI systems". A belief with no exact date and no probability. We read "a few years" as about three from the Oct 26 filing and plot it at 50% as an approximation, as for Hassabis (our inference).
forecasts.gap: A higher skill bar than ours (top experts in most disciplines) and it adds digital control of lab equipment and robots, but it has no learning-on-the-job, any-domain or reliability clause, so neither is clearly easier; 'widely available' means a release, so it can never count a hidden system.
forecasts.rating: expert opinion (lab's own forecast, in Anthropic's S-1 filed with the SEC on Oct 26, 2026 and repeated in its S-1/As of Nov 2 and Nov 10; the wording is checked in all three filings, and the three-year plotting date is our inference)

forecasts.rating: forecast aggregate (Metaculus community prediction, read on the question page at 13:23 PT Nov 13, 2026; about 1.9k forecasters; middle half 5 Feb 2028 to May 2036, from the page's Community row)
forecasts.gapV1: Adds robotics and needs a public announcement, so it can never count a hidden system.

forecasts.who: AI safety leaders survey (Summit on Existential Security)
forecasts.what: AGI (automates >90% of 2025-economy roles), respondents' median 50% year
forecasts.definition: 59 attendees of the 2026 Summit on Existential Security, from the x-risk and AI safety communities, who agreed to share their answers; surveyed Feb 2026, published on the EA Forum Mar 25, 2026. AGI means an AI system or systems that can fully automate more than 90% of roles in the 2025 economy. Median 50% year 2033 and median 25% year 2030 (48 answered); the median year is plotted at mid-year.
forecasts.gap: More than 90% of all roles, physical ones included, so it should come after a system meets our definition, which leaves physical work out.
forecasts.rating: forecast aggregate (survey median of 59 attendees of the 2026 Summit on Existential Security, from the safety community; not a representative sample)
forecasts.gapV1: More than 90% of all roles, physical ones included, so it should come after our bar, which counts remote professional work.

forecasts.what: AGI that most LEAP panelists agree exists, experts' median year if it happens before 2100
forecasts.definition: Wave 8 of FRI's Longitudinal Expert AI Panel, fielded Apr 20 to May 11, 2026 and published Jun 2, 2026, asked for the probability that, before 2100, more than 50% of LEAP panelists will agree AGI exists, and the year if so. AGI is a commercially available AI system that can outperform the 90th percentile professional human employee in every primarily non-physical occupation (based on 2025 performance) on at least 90% of the economically useful non-physical tasks they perform, at an inference cost no more than 5x that of equivalent human labor. The median expert gives 80% that this happens before 2100 and, conditional on it happening, a median year of 2050 (25% by 2039, 75% by 2065); superforecasters give 80% and a median year of 2047. Because the years are conditional, we plot the experts' 2050 at 40% (80% × 50%), at mid-year (our inference).
forecasts.gap: Outperform the 90th-percentile professional on at least 90% of the tasks in every non-physical occupation, at no more than 5x the cost of human labor, and commercially available, so it should come after a system meets our definition; it resolves on most panelists agreeing, so it can never count a hidden system.
forecasts.rating: forecast aggregate (median of FRI's LEAP expert panel, Wave 8, from FRI's own post of Jun 2, 2026; the 40% plotting point is our inference from the conditional median)
